title: Resident Payment Terms for the Utility Pass-Through Service: Channels, Application and Returned Payments
content:
**Clause 1 — Channels and application.** Utility Pass-Through Service statements are paid through the schedule's accepted payment channels, and payments are applied to the oldest unpaid statement first.

**Clause 2 — Certified funds (retired).** The former clause "While the lease the account serves is on certified-funds-only status and its certified-funds end date has not passed, a utility payment is accepted only through the lease's certified-funds channels" is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for accepting utility payments from a lease under a certified-funds restriction.

**Clause 3 — Returned payments.** A returned utility payment is charged back for exactly the returned amount against that payment and carries no returned-payment fee on the utility account.

**Clause 4 — One chargeback per payment.** A payment is charged back only once; a payment that already has a chargeback recorded against it is not charged back again.

**Clause 5 — No suspension.** An unpaid utility balance never leads to suspension of any service by Hearthstone; it is pursued through late fees while the account is open and through collections after the final statement.

## Applying the clauses (hypothetical figures)

**Oldest statement first.** February's statement has 40.00 dollars unpaid and March's 55.00 dollars. A payment of 60.00 dollars clears February's 40.00 and applies the remaining 20.00 to March, leaving 35.00 unpaid on March.

**A returned payment.** The bank returns that 60.00 dollar payment. The account is charged back 60.00 dollars against that payment — not more, and with no returned-payment fee on the utility account. If the same return is reported a second time, no second chargeback is made.

## Basis Q&A

**Does an unpaid utility balance put water or any other service at risk of shut-off?** No. It is pursued through late fees while the account is open and through collections after the final statement.

**Which statement does a payment reduce first?** The oldest unpaid one.
